---
title: "Statistical concepts"
---

The complete concept articles are native R help pages installed with `rulearn`. They work offline in RStudio's Help pane. Enter `library(rulearn)` first, then call `help("topic", package="rulearn")`.

| Topic | Help command |
|---|---|
| Population and sample | `help("population_sample", package="rulearn")` |
| Mean and median | `help("mean_median", package="rulearn")` |
| Variance and standard deviation | `help("standard_deviation", package="rulearn")` |
| Percentiles and quantiles | `help("percentiles_quantiles", package="rulearn")` |
| Probability distributions | `help("probability_distributions", package="rulearn")` |
| Sampling distributions | `help("sampling_distributions", package="rulearn")` |
| Correlation | `help("correlation", package="rulearn")` |
| Autocorrelation | `help("autocorrelation", package="rulearn")` |
| Stationarity | `help("stationarity", package="rulearn")` |
| Hypothesis tests and p-values | `help("p_value", package="rulearn")` |
| Confidence intervals | `help("confidence_intervals", package="rulearn")` |
| Independent and paired data | `help("independent_paired", package="rulearn")` |
| Time series | `help("time_series", package="rulearn")` |
| Trend | `help("trend", package="rulearn")` |
| Recover from R errors | `help("r_errors", package="rulearn")` |
| Seasonality | `help("seasonality", package="rulearn")` |
| Statistical variables vs R objects | `help("statistical_variable", package="rulearn")` |
| Descriptive and inferential statistics | `help("descriptive_inferential", package="rulearn")` |
| Measurement scales | `help("measurement_scales", package="rulearn")` |
| Sample spaces and events | `help("probability_events", package="rulearn")` |
| Independent and conditional events | `help("conditional_independence", package="rulearn")` |

You do not need to remember a title. Use `ru_find("What does a p-value mean?")` to locate it.
